newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco begins plant shutdown after union rejects offer.
newsitem.headline: Inco begins plant shutdown after union rejects offer.

text.p: Nickel giant Inco Ltd said on Sunday it had begun winding down its operations in Thompson, Manitoba, after unionised workers rejected the company's final contract offer.
"We are in the process of turning down the plant," Inco spokesman Dan McSweeney said in a telephone interview.
McSweeney said the plant could not continue to operate without a collective agreement with unionised workers. "The company cannot risk any sudden interruption of operations," he said.
In a vote held earlier on Sunday, the union said 71 percent of those members who voted had rejected Inco's last offer.
About 86 percent of the union's 1,327 members voted on Sunday.
"We are in a legal strike position, but we have not called for strike action," Bob Desjarlai, president of local 6166 of the United Steelworkers of America, said in an interview.
The current three-year contract is set to expire at midnight.
Desjarlai said the union had instructed its members to show up for the night shift and Monday's day shift. He said the union was still interested in negotiating an agreement.
"If they lock us out, then we will deal with it," he said.
The main issues in the labour dispute are pensions, wages, benefits and health and safety.
Inco's Thompson operations produce about 100 million lb of nickel a year in northern Manitoba.
